source.work: Redis documentation, key naming and keyspace patterns
source.locator: data types and key expiry guidance
source.paraphrase: Give every key a namespaced name such as domain:id so keyspace scans, evictions, and deletes stay scoped to one owner.

invariants.why: A bare global key collides with every other feature sharing the database, and a delete or expiry can take down unrelated data.
invariants.fixHint: Name keys as <domain>:<id>, for example session:abc123. Keep the domain next to the module that owns it.
invariants.avoid: Backticks do not add a namespace. A template literal without a colon is still a global key. The call must be on a Redis client: a receiver whose name contains redis or valkey, or a receiver named client, cache, db, kv, store, pub, sub, publisher or subscriber in a file that imports a module whose specifier contains redis, valkey or @vercel/kv. An Express app.get route, a req.get header read and a Map get are not matched. A client under another name is not matched.

source.locator: EX PX EXAT PXAT and KEEPTTL options
source.paraphrase: SET without expiry persists until deletion; persistence is a valid choice for many keys, while sessions and caches may need expiry.

invariants.why: The syntax does not distinguish durable state from sessions. This matcher also treats NX/XX as if they were expiry, which they are not.
invariants.fixHint: Pass { EX: seconds } (or PX/EXAT/PXAT) on every set, or call setEx. NX/XX alone do not bound lifetime.
invariants.avoid: An options object with no expiry field still leaves the key immortal. The expiry must be visible in the call.

source.paraphrase: Channel names share one global bus, so publishers should namespace channels as domain:event to keep subscribers scoped.

invariants.why: A bare channel name collides across features, and a pattern subscriber on updates receives events from every domain that publishes there.
invariants.fixHint: Publish to <domain>:<event>, for example orders:updates. Keep the channel next to the event type it carries.
invariants.avoid: Backticks do not add a namespace. A template channel without a colon collides on the same global bus.

source.paraphrase: KEYS scans the whole keyspace in one blocking call. Production iteration should use SCAN cursors instead.

invariants.why: A KEYS call blocks the single-threaded server while it walks every key, stalling all other clients until it returns.
invariants.fixHint: Iterate with scanIterator (optionally with a MATCH pattern) instead of calling keys.
invariants.avoid: A narrow prefix does not make KEYS cheap. Scope does not change the blocking scan; use SCAN. The call must be on a Redis client: a receiver whose name contains redis or valkey, or a receiver named client, cache, db, kv, store, pub, sub, publisher or subscriber in a file that imports a module whose specifier contains redis, valkey or @vercel/kv. Object.keys and Map keys are not matched. A client under another name is not matched.

source.work: Redis documentation, FLUSHALL and server commands
source.locator: data loss warning on flush commands
source.paraphrase: FLUSHALL, FLUSHDB, CONFIG, and DEBUG reshape or wipe the server. They belong in ops tooling, never in application request paths.

invariants.why: A flush in app code wipes every key for every feature, and a config rewrite from a request handler persists past the deploy that ran it.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the call from app code. Keep flush and config changes in runbooks, migrations, or admin tooling with review.
invariants.avoid: Casing does not make the wipe safe. ioredis spells it flushdb and node-redis flushDb; both are covered.

source.paraphrase: Issuing individual commands sequentially in a loop pays a full TCP round-trip latency per command; batch multi-key reads with MGET or a pipeline.

invariants.why: Sequential await redis.get(k) calls inside a loop turn a 1 ms cache lookup into N serial network round-trips under load.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the loop with a single await redis.mget(...keys) (or redis.mGet(keys) in node-redis) or queue commands on a pipeline.
invariants.avoid: Matches await redis.get / client.get / cache.get inside for, for-in, for-of, while, and do loops. Map.prototype.get is synchronous and not awaited.
